content.title: THE ODD BODY CLUES THAT POINT TO A HIDDEN {{DEFICIENCY}}
facts: **Iodine** – Unexplained weight gain, constant fatigue, dry skin, and a swollen feeling in the front of your neck.
**Vitamin K** – Bruising easily, cuts that take forever to stop bleeding, and bleeding gums when you brush.
**Potassium** – Muscle cramps at night, heart palpitations, and a heavy, weak feeling in your legs.
**Vitamin E** – Numbness or tingling in your hands, blurry vision, and muscle weakness that's hard to explain.
**Folate** – Constant tiredness, irritability, a swollen or sore tongue, and trouble concentrating.
**Zinc** – Slow wound healing, losing your sense of taste or smell, and frequent colds.
**Calcium** – Brittle nails, muscle spasms, numbness around your mouth, and tingling fingertips.
**Follow along** – for more daily health tips like this.
content.caption:
A puffy, swollen feeling in your neck is one of the most overlooked signs of an iodine shortage — your thyroid literally enlarges (a goiter) trying to trap every last bit of iodine it can find to keep making hormones. Easy bruising often points to low vitamin K, since this nutrient is what your liver uses to produce the clotting factors that seal off tiny blood vessel leaks under your skin. And those nighttime leg cramps that jolt you awake? That's frequently a potassium issue — this mineral helps your muscles relax after they contract, so when levels drop, they stay locked in a cramp longer than they should. Everyone's body is different, so use these as a starting point, not a diagnosis.

At @smarthealthfix we focus on four things: nutrition, common symptoms, your organs, and the small daily habits that tie it all together. Our mission is simple — help you notice what your body is trying to tell you, before it turns into a bigger problem.
